review_comments.body: Could this move into `cpp/src/io/mps_writer.cpp` instead? The writer already falls back to `C<id>` / `R<k>` when a names vector is short, but writes an empty entry as a blank name. Treating empty like missing there fixes every caller (Java, Python, C API), and the writer can reuse its `QC` `used_names` logic so a default never collides with a user name such as `C1`.

**Validate quadratic constraint indices before QCMATRIX processing.** The quadratic-constraint setters and `add_quadratic_constraint` accept COO indices without checking them against the variable count. For a one-variable model, `rows={1}` and `cols={1}` can reach the direct `column_names[i]` and `column_names[j]` lookups and cause out-of-bounds access. The merge-base code avoided this regression with bounds-checked `C` fallbacks.

```diff mps_file << "QCMATRIX " << quadratic_row_names[qc_index++] << "\n"; + for (size_t k = 0; k < qc.rows.size(); ++k) { + mps_parser_expects(qc.rows[k] >= 0 && qc.rows[k] < n_variables && + qc.cols[k] >= 0 && qc.cols[k] < n_variables, + error_type_t::ValidationError, + "Quadratic constraint COO index is out of range"); + } typename mps_data_model_t::quadratic_constraint_t qc_canon = qc; ```
